Highlights Last week, US-Iran tensions intensified and broadened, pushing oil prices and inflation fears higher. In the US, stronger-than-expected August inflation raised investor expectations of a Fed rate hike. Meanwhile, the ECB raised rates, Eurozone growth was revised higher, and UK economic activity exceeded expectations. In China, exports strengthened and inflation firmed, while the government announced a major recapitalization of eight banks and insurers. In Japan, wage growth accelerated.    Global equities ended the week lower, while bond yields moved higher, oil prices edged up and the US dollar remained broadly steady.  Rising crack spreads (diesel, fuel oil) and renewed Chinese imports suggest the oil market is tightening amid dwindling global inventories. The demand slowdown that helped briefly balance the market in Q2 has faded. With China back in the market, there is likely no release, leaving higher prices to do the rebalancing work (C.O.T.W). This adds upside pressure to inflation which already printed sticky last week, and the Fed faces a tough decision at this week’s FOMC meeting. Gold will likely be pinched between near-term policy tightening and medium-term risks to equity markets and the economy.
